content.user_title: Build Azure AI Hosted Agents with Python
content.value_statement: Container-based Azure agents require precise SDK, identity, image, and protocol configuration. This skill provides focused Python patterns for creating and managing hosted agents.
actual_capabilities: Installs the required Azure AI Projects and Azure Identity Python packages.
Configures AIProjectClient with DefaultAzureCredential and an Azure project endpoint.
Creates versioned hosted agents from Azure Container Registry images.
Sets protocol versions, CPU, memory, tools, and container environment variables.
Lists and deletes hosted agent versions through the Python SDK.
Provides synchronous, asynchronous, and troubleshooting examples.
limitations: Requires an existing Azure AI project, container image, registry access, and capability host.
Does not build or validate the hosted agent container image.
Does not provision Azure roles, registries, projects, or capability hosts.
Requires environment-specific testing because SDK preview behavior and Azure limits can change.

use_cases.title: Prototype a hosted agent
use_cases.description: Create a first hosted agent version from an existing container image with basic resource settings.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent deployment
use_cases.description: Prepare repeatable SDK patterns for image versions, protocols, tools, and resource allocation.

use_cases.title: Diagnose deployment failures
use_cases.description: Map common hosted agent errors to registry permissions, image paths, capability hosts, and protocol settings.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic hosted agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Python hosted agent named [agent name] using image [image path]. List required Azure resources and configuration values.

prompt_templates.title: Create a hosted agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Python implementation for [agent name] using [image path]. Use DefaultAzureCredential and configure [CPU] CPU with [memory] memory.

prompt_templates.title: Add tools and asynchronous access
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my hosted agent for asynchronous creation. Add [tool list], preserve secure authentication, and explain required container environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my hosted agent design for production. Assess image versioning, permissions, resources, protocols, cleanup, error handling, and secret management.

output_examples.input: Plan a hosted agent for a data processor image with two CPUs and four GiB of memory.
output: Prerequisites: Azure AI project, accessible registry image, managed identity pull permission, and account capability host.
Configuration: Responses protocol version v1, two CPUs, four GiB memory, and a versioned image tag.
Validation: confirm image access, create the agent version, inspect its state, and remove unused versions.

output_examples.input: Explain why my hosted agent reports ImagePullBackOff.
output_examples.output: The project managed identity likely lacks registry pull access. Verify the image path, then grant the identity the AcrPull role.

output_examples.input: Compare synchronous and asynchronous hosted agent creation.
output_examples.output: Both approaches use the same agent definition. The asynchronous pattern also manages credential and client lifecycles with asynchronous context managers.

best_practices: Use immutable image tags for production deployments.
Grant only required registry permissions to the project managed identity.
Store secrets in Azure Key Vault and pass only necessary configuration to containers.
anti_patterns: Do not use the latest image tag for production agent versions.
Do not hardcode credentials or secrets in source code or container definitions.
Do not create agents before validating registry access and capability host configuration.

faq.question: Which Python packages are required?
faq.answer: Install azure-ai-projects version 2.0.0b3 or later and azure-identity.

faq.question: How does the skill authenticate to Azure?
faq.answer: It uses DefaultAzureCredential, which supports local development identities and managed identities.

faq.question: Can this skill build my container image?
faq.answer: No. It expects an existing image in a registry accessible to the Azure project.

faq.question: Which hosted agent protocol is shown?
faq.answer: The examples use the Responses protocol with version v1.

faq.question: Can I configure tools and resources?
faq.answer: Yes. The agent definition supports tools, CPU, memory, protocol versions, image paths, and environment variables.

faq.question: Does the skill support asynchronous Python?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an asynchronous pattern for credentials, the project client, and agent creation.
